newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel grant cuts won't hurt investments.
newsitem.headline: Israel grant cuts won't hurt investments.

text.p: The reduction in government capital investment grants will have a short-term impact on foreign companies, Ministry of Industry and Trade acting director general Joshua Gleitman said on Thursday.
In July the government approved cutting subsidies for capital investments in top priority development areas to a maximum of 20 percent from 34 percent as of January 1.
"Even after the reduction goes into effect we still remain an attractive place to invest particularly for companies in the technology field," Gleitman told Reuters.
He noted that Israel had manpower as well as trade agreements with the European Union and the United States, which made investments attractive.

Israel's Manufacturers' Association said in a statement that in the last five years an average 40 percent of annual investments in Israel were made through the capital investments grant programme. These investments totalled 13.7 billion shekels, the statement said, of a total of 34 billion shekels in the last five years.
The manufacturers said a cut in government grants would hurt investments in development areas.

The ministry is planning only a marginal cut in grants from the Chief Scientist's office for research and development projects. This year the office is expected to make grants totalling $380 million, Gleitman said.
Gleitman, who has retained his post as chief scientist for the ministry, said that next year's proposed budget is $365 million.

However he noted that there was an agreement with the finance ministry that the chief scientist's office would be given an additional $50 million for funding projects which involve several companies that team up to develop a new technology.
